title: LDO (pass device + error amp)
description: A low-dropout regulator sized around its pass device, with the error amplifier represented by its DC gain. The teaching point is the operating point: the dropout spec IS the pass device's $V_{DS}$, so the device is bound at the maximum load current with $V_{DS} = V_{dropout}$, and the dropout invariant just asks that it stays saturated there. The DC loop gain ($A_{ea}*g_{m,pass}*r_{o,pass}$) sets load regulation ($dV_{out}/dI_{load} \approx 1/(A_{ea}*g_{m,pass})$) and the low-frequency PSRR; both are estimates that sim signs off. Quiescent current is budgeted directly. Loop stability (phase margin, the output-pole/ESR-zero placement) is sim-only and not modeled here. Design the error amp itself with an OTA sheet to $A_{req}$ = the loop-gain requirement.

params.name: V_dropout
params.note: dropout voltage; this is the pass device's vds at max load, signed to the table axis

params.name: I_load_max
params.note: maximum load current the pass device carries

params.name: gm_id_pass
params.note: pass-device inversion; higher gm/ID raises loop gain but costs dropout headroom

params.name: L_pass
params.note: longer L raises pass-device ro and DC loop gain

params.name: A_ea
params.note: error-amplifier DC gain; design it with an OTA sheet to the loop-gain requirement

params.name: loadreg_target
params.note: load-regulation budget dVout/dIload (output resistance seen by the load)

params.name: A_loop_min
params.note: minimum DC loop gain for regulation accuracy

rows.name: A_loop
rows.note: DC loop gain: error-amp gain times pass-device intrinsic gain (gm*ro)

rows.name: dVout_dI
rows.note: load regulation: the closed-loop output resistance seen by the load; estimate, sim signs off

rows.name: PSRR_lf_dB
rows.note: low-frequency PSRR ~ the DC loop gain; estimate, sim signs off

rules.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
the pass device must stay saturated within the dropout voltage
error-amp quiescent current under the total budget
estimate-grade; the true output impedance vs frequency and phase margin are sim-owned
DC loop gain for regulation accuracy; estimate-grade
